reason: The picture links these messengers to activating muscle genes in the unspecialized cells, which should start the muscle-cell goal.
expectation: Some cells will begin developing toward muscle cells.

alternatives.reason: The other messengers could start the supporting-fibre goal instead.

effect: The messengers produced muscle precursor cells whose muscle-protein instructions are being copied; the fibres still need to be made.
reaction: The precursor label makes the next stage clearer.
reason: Amino acids are protein building blocks, so they seem useful for making the muscle proteins shown as still to be made.
expectation: The precursor cells will use the amino acids to make muscle proteins.

alternatives.reason: I could start the supporting-cell path instead.

effect: The muscle precursors now contain pulling proteins, completing the muscle goal; the supporting-fibre goal remains.
reaction: The sliding fibres make their pulling job clearer.
reason: The other messengers are pictured activating support-protein genes in the unspecialized cells.
expectation: Some cells will begin developing into supporting cells.

effect: The supporting messengers produced cells with instructions for support proteins, but the fibre network has not been built yet.
reaction: This parallels the muscle-cell path clearly.
reason: Amino acids are protein building blocks, and the cells have instructions for making support proteins.
expectation: The cells will use the amino acids to make supporting fibres.

effect: The supporting cells made fibres around themselves, completing the remaining goal and showing a contrast with proteins kept inside muscle cells.
reaction: The inside-versus-around comparison made the two paths clearer.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making both kinds of protein was worthwhile because it showed how cells with the same DNA can do different jobs: muscle cells keep pulling proteins inside, while supporting cells build fibres around themselves.

leastWorthwhile.text: The second messenger step felt a little repetitive after the muscle path, though the parallel helped make the comparison clear.

surprise.text: I was surprised that cells with the same DNA could make different structures by using different genes.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt arbitrary: the pictures linked each messenger to a cell path, and amino acids were identified as protein building blocks. The details of how the messengers switch genes on were not explained.

continue.text: I would choose to continue, because seeing how these cells become larger tissues sounds interesting, especially after seeing the pulling proteins.
